successCriteria.description: `LeaveRequest` in src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts exposes `reversesRequestId: string | null` as its LAST field (after `cancelledAt`), giving the interface exactly 15 fields; `CreateLeaveRequestInput` remains `Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'>` and therefore also carries the field. No `LeaveRequestEffectiveState` type is declared in this file.

`PgLeaveRequestRepository` persists and reads back `reversesRequestId`: `create` inserts the column (15 values) from `input.reversesRequestId`, and every read path (`findById`, `findByQuery`, `update`'s RETURNING) maps the stored column to `reversesRequestId` on the returned `LeaveRequest` — a row created with a non-null value reads back non-null, and a row created with `null` reads back `null`.

`ILeaveRepository` declares `findByReversesRequestId(reversesRequestId: string, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>` and `PgLeaveRequestRepository` implements it: it returns the matching `LeaveRequest` when a row references the given id, returns `null` (never throws) when none does, and honors the optional trailing `PoolClient` (the query runs on the supplied client when one is passed).
`update` cannot write `reverses_request_id`: `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` and the repository's `FIELD_COLUMNS` map do not gain the field, so no `update` call can set or clear it on an existing row.

`LeaveService.create` supplies `reversesRequestId: null` in the object it passes to `repository.create`, so an original request reverses nothing; no other method of `LeaveService` changes in this phase (in particular `cancel` is untouched and no reversal branch exists yet).

`npm run build` (tsc) is clean, the existing Jest suite passes unchanged (no new test cases added this phase), and `npm run smoke` is green — the `makeRequest` fixture in tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts carries `reversesRequestId: null` so the full `LeaveRequest` literal still type-checks.

constraints: The persisted column name is `reverses_request_id` and the model field is `reversesRequestId`; the column is nullable text and is NULL on an original request, equal to the original's `id` on a reversal row. The model field must be appended LAST (after `cancelledAt`) and the column appended LAST in the repository's column list, so model order and column order stay aligned.

The column is write-once at insert and never updated. `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` (src/shared/types/index.ts) and the repository's `FIELD_COLUMNS` map must NOT gain `reversesRequestId`; `update` must remain structurally unable to write this column. This is what keeps an APPROVED row immutable (GP-008).

The repository must never open BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. `findByReversesRequestId` is read-only and must use the existing private `db(client)` helper so the optional trailing `PoolClient` is honored and the shared pool is the fallback when it is omitted.

`findByReversesRequestId` returns `null` when no row matches and does not throw — the service decides error semantics (a duplicate reversal becomes a ConflictError in Phase 3). No error type is introduced by this phase.

No route, controller, or wire-contract change: `reversesRequestId` serializes with the model, so the existing read endpoints expose it automatically. No new endpoint, no new status code, no change to any request body.

No `LeaveRequestEffectiveState` type is added anywhere in this phase — that value object is derived, never persisted, and is not part of this feature's file set. No new module, no new cross-module dependency edge, and no change to `src/shared/types/index.ts`.
Strict TypeScript: no `any` (use `unknown` with type guards), no implicit any, strict null checks. No direct DB access outside the repository layer (GP-001). No hardcoded secrets.
outOfScope: The APPROVED reversal branch in `LeaveService.cancel` (inserting the new CANCELLED row, releasing the balance once, the duplicate-reversal ConflictError, the CANCEL audit entry and the notification) — Phase 3. `cancel` must not be touched this phase.
New test cases for the reversal path (immutability, single release, terminality) — Phase 4. This phase only keeps the existing suite compiling and green.
The real-Postgres smoke stage proving the reversal end-to-end — Phase 5. `scripts/smoke.js` is not modified this phase.

Any change to the migration from Phase 1 (migrations/20260914000001_add_reverses_request_id_to_leave_requests.js) — it is read as a dependency, not edited. Also out of scope: any query filter or server-side collapsing of reversal rows in `findByQuery`, and any change to `leave.routes.ts`.

ambiguities.description: Whether `findByReversesRequestId` should be added to the repository interface only, or also surfaced through the service/route layer in this phase.
options: Repository interface + implementation only (service consumes it in Phase 3)
Also expose a service method now

ambiguities.description: Whether the `makeRequest` fixture in the leave service test constructs a full `LeaveRequest` literal (requiring the new field) or a partial/overrides object (requiring no change).
Whether the repository's `COLUMNS` constant should be a single string (current shape) or split into a list; the new column must be appended last either way.
options: Keep the existing single concatenated string, append the column last

entityInvariants.invariant: A row is either an ORIGINAL request (`reversesRequestId` null) or a REVERSAL of one (`reversesRequestId` = the original's `id`). Both are the same entity type with the same 15-field shape; the field is the only discriminator. The persisted lifecycle state set is unchanged (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) — no new persisted status is introduced. The field is set once at insert and never mutated afterwards.

The canonical shape is a cross-module data contract: no existing field may be renamed, retyped, reordered, or removed, and no field may be added other than `reversesRequestId`. `CreateLeaveRequestInput` stays `Omit<LeaveRequest, 'id'>` — its form does not change, it only inherits the new field.

The persisted row must round-trip: a value written to `reverses_request_id` at insert is returned unchanged by every read path, and a NULL is returned as `null` (never `undefined`, never a synthesized value). The repository never derives or defaults the field.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: None at this layer — the repository performs no authorization; role-scoped visibility stays in the service (GP-005).
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Read-only. Returns the matching LeaveRequest, or `null` when no row references the given id. Never throws for absence; never opens BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK. Honors the optional trailing PoolClient (falls back to the shared pool when omitted).

Signature and error semantics unchanged. It now persists `input.reversesRequestId` (nullable) and returns the persisted row including it. A unique-index violation on `reverses_request_id` surfaces as the driver's error and is left to the caller's transaction to roll back — the repository does not translate it.

interfaceConstraints.operation: ILeaveRepository.update(id: string, changes: UpdateLeaveRequestDto, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest>
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unchanged: NotFoundError(404) when the row is missing (both the empty-changes branch and the zero-affected-row branch). It must remain unable to write `reverses_request_id` — the field is absent from `UpdateLeaveRequestDto` and from `FIELD_COLUMNS`.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The model field name, nullability and position must match the reconciled entity shape exactly: `reversesRequestId: string | null` appended last after `cancelledAt`, giving the canonical 15-field `LeaveRequest`.

The repository's column list, row type, `mapRow` mapping and INSERT value list must stay in the same order and cover the same 15 columns as the model — `reverses_request_id` appended last, matching the model field order, so `mapRow` and the INSERT cannot drift apart.

The persisted column must match the Phase 1 migration: nullable text `reverses_request_id`, NULL on an original, equal to the original's `id` on a reversal, write-once, with the unique partial index on non-null values as the exactly-once guarantee. The repository must not assume a NOT NULL constraint or a foreign key.

`UpdateLeaveRequestDto` must remain unchanged — it must NOT gain `reversesRequestId` — so the repository's `FIELD_COLUMNS` map (typed `Record<keyof UpdateLeaveRequestDto, string>`) stays exhaustive and `update` stays unable to write the column.

`LeaveService.create` must supply `reversesRequestId: null` in the `CreateLeaveRequestInput` literal it builds, matching the existing literal's field order and null conventions (an original request reverses nothing). No other line of the service changes.

The `makeRequest` fixture must construct a complete `LeaveRequest` literal including `reversesRequestId: null`, so the fixture stays assignable to the 15-field interface and `tsc` stays clean. No new test cases are added.

integrationPoints.why: Phase 1's migration is the schema contract this phase maps: the column name, nullability and write-once semantics must match it exactly, and the unique partial index is the exactly-once guarantee the later reversal branch relies on.
The repository's `FIELD_COLUMNS` is typed against `UpdateLeaveRequestDto`; leaving the DTO unchanged is what structurally prevents `update` from writing the new column.
The only consumer of `CreateLeaveRequestInput` today; it must supply the new field as null or the build breaks. It is also the seam Phase 3 extends with the reversal branch.
No change is required: `reversesRequestId` serializes with the model, so the existing read endpoints expose it automatically. The route layer must not be touched.
`findByReversesRequestId` must accept the optional trailing `PoolClient` so Phase 3 can call it inside the service-owned transaction; the repository never opens the transaction itself.
